"Feeling the Sorrow of Others" in a Tale by Saadi

In the story of the Damascus famine, Saadi speaks of a man who is not himself in financial hardship, yet the suffering of the hungry robs him of pleasure. Can one, in times of war, economic hardship, and insecurity, both worry about the suffering of others and continue living?

In this episode, inspired by Saadi's tale, we explore the meaning of empathy in difficult days; we speak about the necessity of compassion and reducing the suffering of others, and we reflect on how the flood of images of suffering on social media can gradually desensitize us. In this segment, we will also seek answers to these questions: Is happiness in times of hardship a sign of indifference, and how can discontent become a criterion for judging others?

Taqi Pournamdarian is a literary scholar, a prominent researcher of Persian literature, and a professor at the University of Tehran, who has devoted an important part of his scholarly life to the study of mystical poetry and the thought of Iranian mystics. He is considered one of the leading figures in the study of mysticism and literary criticism in contemporary Iran, and his research on Rumi, Hafez, and the symbolic language of mystical texts holds a special place in literary studies. Among his well-known works are "Ramz va Dastan-haye Ramzi dar Adab-e Farsi" (Symbol and Symbolic Tales in Persian Literature), "Didari ba Simorgh" (A Visit with the Simorgh), and "Gomshode-ye Lab-e Darya" (The Lost One at the Edge of the Sea). With a precise and methodical approach, Pournamdarian has examined the semantic layers, symbols, and intellectual structures of mystical poetry and prose, and has also played an influential role in training researchers of Persian literature.@sahandiranmehr

Death of Dr. Pirouz Mojtahedzadeh; Professor and Researcher of Political Geography and Geopolitics of Iran

Dr. Pirouz Mojtahedzadeh, professor and researcher of political geography and geopolitics of Iran, passed away in the early hours of today in London.

Dr. Pirouz Mojtahedzadeh, a political geographer and renowned Iranian researcher, was one of the figures who devoted an important part of his scholarly and research work to Iran's political geography, border issues, the Persian Gulf, and Iran's geopolitical position in the region. His name is linked to discussions concerning Iran's territorial integrity, the three islands, and the strategic importance of the Persian Gulf.

Throughout his scholarly career, Mojtahedzadeh contributed to discussions on political geography and Iran's national interests through authoring books and publishing articles and specialized viewpoints — a field in which knowledge of history, geography, and power relations is of fundamental importance for understanding Iran's position in the region. He was among the researchers who spent their lives studying Iran's land, history, and political situation. May his memory be cherished, and may his loss be condoled to his family, friends, academic colleagues, and the scholarly community of Iran.

@sahandiranmehr

"A rogue carried a log into his house,
He flung it down and squeezed himself inside.
He spotted a dagger at its waist, that wretch,

It said, 'If anyone harbors a single evil thought against me,
I'll rip his belly open.'
